surfaceContracts.source: GET /api/notifications and GET /api/notifications/unread-count with source envelopes, filters, pagination, broadcasts, expiry, and read semantics
surfaceContracts.targetObserved: The frontend exposes GET-only list and unread-count BFF routes with explicit HEAD-to-405 overrides; all other non-GET methods are rejected. List permits only bounded status/limit/offset, forwards only a verified bearer, streams at most 2 MiB, parses the same bytes into exact wire and passthrough JSON values, applies bounded identity/recipient/text/data/action fields, and cross-checks every current-target row against the principal wallet; unread-count streams at most 4 KiB and requires the exact non-negative current-target DTO. SSR preserves explicit outcomes without sample fallback, admits only canonical all/read/unread status plus all ten bounded source notification types, five priorities, RFC3339 start/end dates, and derived page/offset semantics, while the Dioxus page renders native status/type/priority links, preserves date filters through pagination, and exposes bounded owner actions through the Rust BFF without inferring delivery. Cookie-backed mutations require same-origin context, bearer integrations remain cryptographically verified, and the route-scoped controller accepts only a closed action map with bounded IDs, exact {ok:true} responses, no-store credentials, and truthful error/reload states. The active shared header starts empty, hidden, and unavailable; only a server-verified authenticated non-offline response receives its unread-count controller. Authenticated HTML and every list/count BFF outcome are private/no-store, and the fetch bypasses caches. The unread controller uses the exact route with credentials, exact-object/non-negative-safe-integer validation, stale-response generation guards, zero/error hiding, AA badge contrast, a 99+ visual cap with the exact count in the accessible label, and text-only DOM writes. Local authenticated and responsive browser smoke now prove owner-route authentication and native layout; source method/query/envelope/broadcast/expiry/read parity and non-local runtime proof remain blocked.

ownershipRules.rule: Every owner read or mutation derives the normalized wallet solely from the verified principal and hides foreign IDs with 404.
Admin reads and mutations use explicit operation permissions; manage does not silently grant unrelated read, delivery, or template authority.
Domain publishers use a non-browser internal service identity scoped to approved event types and recipient derivation rules.
user_id, wallet recipient, email recipient, broadcast, plan targeting, and channel cannot contradict one another.
Broadcast and plan fanout require explicit authorization, audience resolution, bounded cardinality, and auditable actor identity.

deliveryRules.rule: Persist the notification and delivery jobs atomically before any transport dispatch.
Notification read state, per-channel delivery state, provider acceptance, client acknowledgement, click state, and terminal failure are independent fields.
SMTP/provider acceptance is not user delivery; absent provider configuration must never report sent.
In-app success requires durable persistence; realtime fanout is best-effort and replayable from durable state.
Transient errors use bounded exponential backoff with jitter; permanent errors terminate without retry.
Exhausted jobs enter a queryable dead-letter state with redrive authorization and audit history.
SSE replay uses a durable monotonic cursor or Last-Event-ID policy and deduplicates reconnect delivery.
Preferences, quiet hours, legal/security exceptions, expiry, and channel eligibility are evaluated by the backend before jobs are created.

idempotencyRules.rule: Publisher requests require an idempotency key scoped to service principal and event type with a request hash.
Domain delivery is unique by source event identity, recipient, template/version, and channel.
Workers claim jobs with leases and compare-and-set transitions so crashes cannot produce uncontrolled duplicate sends.
Provider message IDs and accepted responses are recorded for deduplication and reconciliation.
Read/unread/delete/bulk operations are retry-safe and return stable affected-count semantics.

privacyRules.rule: Logs and traces never contain message bodies, template variables, email addresses, tokens, or raw provider payloads.
Template rendering is strict, size-bounded, allowlisted, and safe for text and HTML contexts.
Action and image URLs are restricted to approved schemes/origins and cannot create script or tracking injection.
Retention, expiry, user deletion, legal hold, and account erasure semantics are explicit per channel.
SMTP, push, Redis, database, and internal identity secrets come from managed secrets and are never accepted in browser payloads.

migrationRequirements: declare the canonical source and target schemas and one write authority
use additive versioned migrations rather than startup DDL
backfill wallet_notifications, read/click/delivery fields, preferences, templates, and publisher event identities
preserve normalized wallet ownership and broadcast semantics
run count, checksum, state-distribution, orphan, and duplicate reconciliation
support resumable batches with checkpoints and bounded locks
prove forward compatibility, rollback compatibility, and no destructive migration without reviewed necessity
observabilityRequirements: queue depth and oldest-job age by channel
enqueue, attempt, provider-acceptance, terminal-failure, retry, and dead-letter counters
SSE active connections, reconnects, lag, replay count, and fanout failures
preference suppressions and invalid-recipient metrics without PII labels
template render failures and version distribution
alerts and runbooks for delivery lag, error budget, dead letters, reconciliation drift, and provider outages
cutoverRequirements: shadow reads compare source and target without exposing target results
publisher canary uses explicit allowlisted event types and tenants/wallets
single-writer switch is configuration-controlled and audited
rollback preserves idempotency and does not replay already accepted provider sends
SSE clients reconnect across the switch without losing or duplicating durable events
legacy writes are disabled only after reconciliation and rollback-window approval

blockers.summary: The executable compatibility-route audit now verifies all reviewed BFF and service method/path registrations, and guarded local compatibility plus authenticated owner/admin browser smokes validate owner list/count/preferences envelopes, owner authentication, a foreign-owner 404, responsive native controls, and the permissioned admin inventory projection through the live Rust/Dioxus BFFs. A dedicated BFF adapter now exposes the pinned development `/api/notifications` list/count/preferences and owner mutation paths, maps target IDs and envelopes, binds source type/priority policy metadata into the backend-owned preference document, and rejects caller-controlled foreign wallet selectors. Source push status/nested-subscription/owner-wide-unsubscribe aliases now project the source-specific operation envelopes, including bulk updated/deleted counts; source SSE aliases translate owner-bound UUID-compatible frames and reconnect cursors while rejecting unsupported filters and non-UUID target IDs. Complete SSE broadcast/plan-ID parity, legacy status semantics, provider delivery, and broader live integration remain unproven.
blockers.resolution: Implement an explicit adapter or versioned API and contract-test every A11 surface against the pinned source behavior.

blockers.summary: The candidate now has an exact static notifications/templates shape plus an explicit allowlist for the three base checks and eight lifecycle foreign keys, and guarded loopback/runtime audits prove clean ordering, populated legacy-row preservation, service readiness, and worker transitions. The legacy dry-run mapper now validates and counts bounded wallet, title/body, type/priority, channels, action/data, and RFC3339 expiry/creation projection fields without writing target rows; source reconciliation and production adoption remain unproven.
blockers.resolution: Choose one schema authority, add versioned mappings and populated upgrade steps, then prove clean-database plus upgraded-database behavior.

blockers.summary: Runtime DDL and startup seeds are statically removed, and the guarded local audit proves clean/populated ordering plus dump/restore recovery; the pre-existing migration history remains unsafe/ambiguous and production adoption is unproven.
blockers.resolution: Repair and adopt the reviewed migration history, prove clean and populated upgrade paths, and keep startup free of DDL and sample writes.

blockers.summary: Direct owner authentication now rejects unknown owner-list fields, unsupported delivery statuses, conflicting type aliases, malformed dates, reversed ranges, and out-of-range pagination; the backend query applies bounded type, priority, date, read/unread/all, expiry, and broadcast predicates. Normalization, foreign-resource behavior, source envelope parity, and broader owner contract parity remain unproven.
blockers.resolution: Lock canonical wallet normalization and owner-scoped integration tests for every single and bulk operation.

blockers.summary: Owner read/unread now updates engagement state without changing delivery status, owner acknowledgement persists separately, click/dismiss persist idempotent first-event timestamps, and the Rust frontend BFF forwards those events with verified bearer/request identity while exposing legacy PUT/DELETE aliases over the Rust-owned service mutations; cookie-backed browser mutations now require same-origin context, and the Dioxus notifications page renders bounded row/bulk controls through a closed Rust-served action map with explicit error/reload states. A guarded local mutation browser audit now exercises mark-read, acknowledgement, and disposable delete through the authenticated Dioxus page, while source parity, legal-hold integration, and complete independent lifecycle integration remain missing. Additive expiry filtering, worker terminal-expiry checks, and a guarded local owner-delete audit ordering dependent cleanup now exist.
blockers.resolution: Define independent channel delivery and user engagement state machines with guarded transitions and exact affected-row checks.

blockers.summary: Owner notification preferences are durably validated and persisted, and owner-bound enqueue paths retain disabled-channel suppression plus PostgreSQL-known timezone-aware quiet-hour release; a guarded local handler audit proves timezone validation, quiet-hour calculation, owner-bound push subscribe/revoke, endpoint ownership rejection, and suppression without a channel job. The authenticated Dioxus account view now has a bounded same-origin Rust form adapter with explicit SSR save/error states, and the authenticated local mutation browser audit saves and reloads a real timezone preference while confirming push fails closed without VAPID material. Real provider delivery, exception policy, and worker/reconnect integration remain incomplete.
blockers.resolution: Exercise the native settings form in an authenticated browser, document legal/security exceptions, and prove preference suppression and release across live database, worker, provider, and reconnect tests.

blockers.summary: The extracted service now exposes owner-authenticated SSE with durable cursors, acknowledgement, keepalive, bounded connections, and optional Redis wake-up fanout; a guarded local two-listener audit proves one wake-up reaches independent instances, local replay survives a bounded Redis failure, and both listeners recover after an ephemeral broker restart, while durable SSE disconnect/reconnect, browser receipt, and staging evidence remain unproven.
blockers.resolution: Implement principal-bound streaming with bounded connections, keepalive, origin policy, backpressure, and disconnect cleanup.

blockers.summary: Durable owner replay cursors, Last-Event-ID validation, reconnect dedupe, acknowledgement, and an additive expiry projection/filter now exist; local two-listener Redis fanout, bounded loss fallback, and ephemeral broker restart recovery are covered, but live expiry/cleanup/replay proof, durable browser reconnect receipt, and staging evidence remain incomplete.
blockers.resolution: Define replay ordering and Last-Event-ID semantics backed by durable state and idempotent acknowledgement.

blockers.summary: Owner-scoped push status/subscribe/revoke storage, bounded VAPID key lineage, the account-only Dioxus permission control, and Rust-served worker payload/action validation now exist behind configured active/previous key pairs; a loopback provider audit proves encrypted Web Push/VAPID acceptance and stable provider IDs, and authenticated/responsive local browser smoke proves the control fails closed when VAPID material is absent. blockers.summary: The extracted admin send now requires a canonical wallet user_id, binds in-app recipients to that wallet, validates email/push recipient shapes, rejects broadcast/all and inline/template contradictions, and checks template/channel agreement. blockers.resolution: Use transactional outboxes at all producers, server-side recipient resolution, and atomic notification+job creation with post-commit fanout.

blockers.summary: Publisher request/event and channel-job identities are now scoped and persisted, migrated producers use a bounded one-retry helper that reuses stable source event IDs, and both remote and in-process paths reject deterministic-ID payload mismatches; a guarded local admission failure audit proves partial idempotency/inbox/outbox writes roll back together, successful SMTP attempts persist a deterministic job-derived Message-ID, and a guarded local callback audit proves signed provider reconciliation, replay deduplication, and terminal-state reorder protection. blockers.summary: Durable per-channel jobs, lease transitions, bounded retry classification/backoff with jitter, final-attempt terminal/dead-letter conversion, and authorized redrive now exist; guarded local audits prove retry-attempt persistence, dead-letter transition, redrive, expired-lease reclamation, signed provider callback reconciliation, callback replay deduplication, terminal-state reorder protection, and acceptance of callbacks signed by both active and previous rotation keys, while external provider recovery, route-level authorization, and staging crash-recovery drills remain incomplete.
